questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about conditions just ahead. This sign warns you that the road curves to the right.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Let any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in the intersection go first.
Let only pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in the intersection go first.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction the arrow points. But first, let any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection pass safely.

questions.question: You must use your low beams when:
questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights to use with low beams.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and give the right-of-way to others.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, check that the way is clear, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders have the right to:

options.text: Use half of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use one full traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can use a full lane. Two motorcycles can share one lane if they want. Do not pass a motorcycle while staying in the same lane.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make space for them to merge, if you can.
Speed up to keep them from merging.
Stay in your lane no matter what.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make space for them to merge, if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room in your lane to let other vehicles merge.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Mirrors do not show everything behind your car. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to be sure the lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to be sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: Strong wind on highways:

options.text: Only reduces how far you can see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers. It can reduce visibility by blowing dust onto the road and can also push vehicles sideways.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Cross two lanes at the same time.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap big enough to safely merge into traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to enter.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A triangular red and white sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving. It is a leading cause of traffic crashes. Distractions prevent drivers from seeing and hearing important warning signs that help avoid accidents.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. You should:

options.text: Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make constant visual checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spot or be missed in a quick glance. Always look carefully for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you stops in your lane with red lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and proceed when you think all children have exited the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.
Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. Exception: You do not need to stop if the bus is on the other side of a divided highway.

questions.question: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, use your headlights:

options.text: So others can see your vehicle.
To warn others of bad weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: So others can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your vehicle easier to spot. Turn on your low beams anytime you use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you, glance toward the right edge of the road instead of looking straight ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road until you pass the other car.

questions.question: In rain, you should be most careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. At this time, oil from cars mixes with rain and creates a slippery surface.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
More slowly than the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless the traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange color is used for construction and maintenance area warning signs.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: You can eliminate them by having one outside mirror on each side of your vehicle.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
You can check blind spots by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots. Other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward them.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming cars. You can only turn when it is safe and the oncoming traffic is not affected.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. How can you let other drivers know you are there?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers may not see you. Turn on your low beam headlights if you are using your windshield wipers.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: How can you help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after you start down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you do not know what is ahead. Braking on a curve may cause you to skid.
